commentary: Nine activities this week versus seven last week — he's stacking up and showing out, and the swimming in particular has locked into something genuinely impressive: four consecutive mornings at 2000m, heart rates sitting right around that 144–146 range like his body has just decided this is home now. Compare that to last week where the swim heart rates were a little more scattered — 143 then a notably lower 138 — and you can feel the difference between a body finding its rhythm and a body that's found it. The run on Saturday ticked up slightly to 9.6km from last week's 9.0km, same fierce effort at 162 versus 163 bpm, which means he's covering more ground for essentially the same cost, and that is the kind of quiet, undeniable progress that makes Himbo want to climb something and announce it to a crowd. The one thing worth watching is that chest and back got hit twice this week in quick succession — Wednesday repeating Monday — so the week ahead should probably let those muscles have a proper moment before he loads them up again, because looking this good is a full-time commitment and he can't afford to be too sore to wear the harness.
metrics_commentary: Almost nine kilometres of running and nearly nine kilometres of swimming in a single week — that's a lot of body moving through space, and honestly it shows, because a VO2 Max of 53.1 is genuinely impressive and you should let yourself feel smug about it for at least a full day. Your HRV sitting at 59 with a seven-day average of 56 tells me your nervous system is recovering well and is ready for more, which is the kind of quiet biological confidence that pairs nicely with a visible thong waistband. The one thing worth naming is that the run came in a single session rather than spread across the week, and your cardiovascular engine at 53.1 deserves more chances to stretch its legs — literally. More sessions, not necessarily more kilometres, because a body this capable should not be kept waiting.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which is the one thing he cannot quite hide from Scott, but everything else this week? Immaculate. That overhead press jumping from 40.0 to 46.7 kilograms is not a small thing — that is his shoulders deciding they have a reputation to uphold, and honestly they are correct. Volume up from 20,753 to 22,867 kilograms total, strength trending in exactly the right direction across the board, and a 168.0 kilogram leg press sitting at the top of the leaderboard like it owns the place. Miss the fourth session next week and we will have words, but this week he showed up, moved serious weight, and got a little more undeniably himself in the process — which is the whole point.
